# find-gmail-filter

<!-- Generated By: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) -->

Lists every Gmail filter that matches a given message, identified by its `Message-ID` header.

## Overview

- Prints each matching filter as a numbered block: its criteria, then its actions (archive, label, forward, ...), one per line, in the order Gmail returns filters
- Reports all matches, not just the first
- Gmail's search engine decides each match: every filter's criteria is converted to a search query and run as `rfc822msgid:<id> (<filter query>)`, including spam and trash
- Uses the [`gws` CLI](https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli) for all Gmail API calls

### Limitations

- Search runs against the message's current state, not its state at delivery. Criteria such as `is:unread` or `label:` can differ from what the filter saw when it fired.
- `negatedQuery` ("Doesn't have") is rendered as `-(text)`, per the API description. Gmail's UI renders it as `-{text}`; with several words the two differ, and which one the filter engine applies has not been verified.
- One API call per filter, plus one to confirm the message exists. Searches run in parallel (`--jobs`); a rate-limit error from Gmail fails the run rather than retrying, so lower `--jobs` if that happens.

## Installation

Requires `gws` authenticated with the `gmail.readonly` scope (covers both `messages.list` and `settings.filters.list`):

```bash
gws auth login --readonly -s gmail
make install-pipx
```

## Usage

```bash
find-gmail-filter '<CAF1234abcd@mail.gmail.com>'
```

Angle brackets are optional. Each match prints with Gmail's filter-editor field names; long values wrap to the terminal width under the value column:

```text
Filter 1
    From:           alerts@example.com
    Actions:        Skip the Inbox (archive it)
                    Mark as read
                    Apply label: Alerts/Prod

Filter 2
    Has the words:  list:one.example.com OR list:two.example.com OR
                    list:three.example.com
    Has attachment: yes
    Actions:        Forward to: archive@example.org
```

Label IDs in actions are resolved to names with one extra `labels.list` call, made only when something matched.

Options: `-j/--jobs N` (parallel searches, default 8), `--debug`, `-q/--quiet`, `--log-file PATH`. A `Matched N of M filters` summary goes to stderr; no stdout output means no filter matched. Exit code 1 when `gws` fails or no message has that `Message-ID`.

## Development

```bash
make check
```
